title: AI-Native Professional: Workflows & Agents for Everyday Productivity
summary: Use AI assistants, reusable prompt systems, and lightweight agents to improve everyday professional workflows.
capstone: Personal productivity agent stack with documented time-savings measurement.
prerequisites: Basic digital literacy; no coding required
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a personal task workspace.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a personal task workspace.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a productivity workflow design portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a personal task workspace.
activity.overview: You support a personal task workspace. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?

activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.
